Today you draft the layout on paper. Polish happens next week.

## A2 size, in plain language

A2 is **240 mm by 594 mm**. Read from two metres away.

* Title text, **50 pt or larger**.
* Body text, **20 pt or larger**.
* One dominant figure, not five small ones.
* Plenty of white space.
* Most weak posters have **too much text**.

## The seven-box rule

Take an A4 sheet. Divide into seven labelled regions.

| Box | Content |
|-----|---------|
| Title | Package name, both authors |
| The problem | Two sentences, no jargon |
| The solution | One sentence stating what the package does |
| Code example | Six lines showing the simplest use |
| Figure | Map, chart, or table from the demo notebook |
| Design choices | Three bullets (CRS choice, data choice, scope) |
| Links | TestPyPI URL, GitHub URL, contact |

If you cannot fill a box, you do not yet know what goes there. That is the point.

## A common failure mode

Posters that try to **explain everything** look like dense walls of text. Nobody reads them.

A working poster answers three questions in 30 seconds.

* What problem does this solve?
* What does the package look like in practice?
* Where can I find it?

Everything else is for the conversation, not the poster.

## Installing from TestPyPI with `--extra-index-url`

When installing your package from TestPyPI, use `--extra-index-url` instead of `-i`:

```bash
pip install your-package --extra-index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/
```

### Why not `-i`?

```bash
# -i replaces the default index entirely — pip ONLY looks at TestPyPI
pip install your-package -i https://test.pypi.org/simple/

# --extra-index-url adds TestPyPI as a second index alongside PyPI
pip install your-package --extra-index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/
```

With `-i`, pip **only** looks at TestPyPI. If your package depends on `pandas` or `geopandas`, pip cannot find them because they are not on TestPyPI.

With `--extra-index-url`, pip checks **both** TestPyPI (for your package) **and** PyPI (for everything else). Always prefer `--extra-index-url` when installing from a custom repository.
